subject.title: Control UI: Config upgrade/hardening suggestions should apply changes automatically with before/after diff and user acceptance, not direct users to edit files manually

question: Which Control UI security/auth recommendations may be applied automatically, and what confirmation, audit, restart, and allowlist policy must wrap those config.patch writes?
rationale: The source shows the write primitive exists, but deciding when the UI may turn hardening advice into an executable auth/config change is a product and security boundary rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Allowlisted Recommendation Actions
options.body: Permit a narrow set of maintainer-approved recommendations to propose config.patch changes with a before/after diff, explicit acceptance, audit note, and restart messaging.

options.title: Manual Guidance Only
options.body: Keep security-sensitive recommendations as docs and copyable config snippets, accepting the current support burden and UX friction.

options.title: Defer To Shared Protected-Config Flow
options.body: Wait for a broader protected config approval model before adding Control UI-specific apply actions.

recommendation.title: Allowlisted Recommendation Actions
recommendation.body: Permit a narrow set of maintainer-approved recommendations to propose config.patch changes with a before/after diff, explicit acceptance, audit note, and restart messaging.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses recent Control UI login recovery, Settings UX, and security/default policy where steipete has the strongest observed history signal.
